front: State the standard TEE probe frequency for adult imaging.
back: 5–7 MHz — higher than TTE (2–5 MHz) because the target is closer to the transducer (behind the esophageal wall), permitting higher frequency without penetration loss.

front: Which TEE view is best for interrogating the mitral valve for MitraClip placement?
back: Mid-esophageal LAX (125–135°) and intercommissural views (50–70°). Real-time 3D TEE is central for MitraClip: 3D en-face 'surgeon's view' of the mitral valve is used to align the clip perpendicular to the coaptation line.

front: Which TEE view is best for interrogating the left atrial appendage?
back: Mid-esophageal 2Ch view (90°) and multiple angles from 0–140° with off-axis rotation. LAA velocity is measured with PW at the LAA orifice.

front: What is the primary indication for intraoperative TEE during CABG?
back: 1) Confirmation of adequate air removal from cardiac chambers after cardiopulmonary bypass. 2) Assessment of new regional wall-motion abnormalities suggesting graft failure. 3) Quantification of pre- and post-op MR and other valvular pathology.

front: How is ICE positioned during PFO/ASD closure?
back: ICE catheter is advanced through the femoral vein to the RA and rotated to visualize the interatrial septum. Provides real-time guidance for transseptal puncture (if needed) and confirmation of device position.
